questions.q: A validation rule's formula returns TRUE. What happens?
options: The record saves normally
The record is deleted
The save is blocked and the error message is shown, because TRUE means the data is invalid
The rule is deactivated automatically
questions.explain: Validation rule formulas return TRUE for invalid data, which blocks the save and displays the error message.

questions.q: Which formula correctly blocks an Opportunity from being Closed Won without an Amount?
options: AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"), ISBLANK(Amount))
AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName, "Closed Won"), NOT(ISBLANK(Amount)))
ISBLANK(StageName)
ISPICKVAL(Amount, "Closed Won")
questions.explain: The rule must be TRUE when the stage is Closed Won and Amount is blank. ISPICKVAL is used for picklist fields such as StageName.

questions.q: What happens to a Data Loader row that fails a validation rule?
options: It is loaded anyway, and the rule is ignored for bulk loads
It is silently dropped with no record of the failure
The whole Salesforce org is locked until it is fixed
It is rejected and written to the error file with the rule's message, while other rows can still load
questions.explain: Validation rules apply to API and Data Loader saves; failed rows appear in the error output.

questions.q: Does a new validation rule fix existing records that already break it?
options: Yes, it automatically corrects all existing records
No. It only runs when a record is created or updated, so existing bad data needs to be found with SOQL
Yes, but only for records created by Data Loader
No, and it also cannot be used on custom objects
questions.explain: Rules fire on save. Existing violations remain until audited (for example with SOQL) and corrected.

questions.q: What is the safest way to prepare for a large load into an org with validation rules?
options: Delete all validation rules permanently before every load
Load everything at once in production and check for errors afterward
Test the load in a sandbox and review the error file, only bypassing rules deliberately through an approved mechanism
Rename the CSV file so the rules do not apply
questions.explain: Testing in a sandbox reveals which rows fail. Any bypass, such as a custom permission, should be a deliberate, controlled choice.
